'''Longbow Sharpshot''' is a [[Arcane Enhancement#Primary_Weapon_Arcanes|Primary Arcane]] for bows that, on landing a [[Enemy Body Parts|weak point]] hit, increases the [[damage]] of the next shot.

==Effect==
{| class="emodtable"
|-
![[Arcane Enhancement#Rank|Rank]]
!Damage Bonus
|-
|0||50%
|-
|1||100%
|-
|2||150%
|-
|3||200%
|-
|4||250%
|-
|5||300%
|}
==Acquisition==
*May appear as a [[The Steel Path|Steel Path]] [[The Circuit|Circuit]] Tier 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, or 8 reward on a weekly rotational basis.
*May be sold by [[Acrithis]] for 20 {{Resource|Pathos Clamp}} on a daily rotational basis, requiring [[Drifter/Intrinsics|Drifter Intrinsics]] [[Drifter/Intrinsics/Opportunity|Opportunity]] Rank 9 for the arcanes to appear in her shop.
*May drop from Undercroft portals in the [[Duviri]] Experience while on [[The Steel Path]] (2.78%).

==Notes==
*[[Trading]] Longbow Sharpshot requires the trader to be [[Mastery Rank]] 11 or higher.
*Damage bonus is '''multiplicative''' to mods like {{M|Serration}}.
*Cannot be equipped on crossbows such as {{Weapon|Attica}}, {{Weapon|Nagantaka}} ({{Weapon|Nagantaka Prime|Prime}}), and {{Weapon|Zhuge}} ({{Weapon|Zhuge Prime|Prime}}).
*As long as every consecutive shot is a weak point hit, the buff is always active.
*If the buff is not active, the first weak point hit does not benefit from it, even if the bow has multishot.
*Where {{M|Galvanized Aptitude}} adds with damage mods, {{PAGENAME}} will '''not''' multiply [[GunCO]]'s bonus portion.
**Explanation: {{M|Galvanized Aptitude}} does not always add with damage mods like {{M|Serration}}, but with weapon cases where it does add such as {{Weapon|Daikyu}}, Galvanized Aptitude's entire contribution to damage is a recalculation of all bonuses minus +damage, thus making it mathematically additive to that particular bonus. However, this recalculation is outdated and does not include many damage bonuses, one of which is Longbow Sharpshot's multiplying effect. Its <u>additive</u> formula regarding Longbow Sharpshot is as follows:
***'''Damage bonus% = [(1 + Serration) {{mul}} (1 + Longbow Sharpshot)] + Galvanized Aptitude'''

***We needed to address an issue with exploitative Legendary Arcanes farming and ban-evasion account creation used to trade Legendary Arcanes. Other options we experimented with had the risk of innocent players getting caught in the crossfire of the ban-evasion subjects. When we took a look at Trading stats we found that a very small number of players below Mastery Rank 10 trade Legendary Arcanes, and therefore decided to go this route. This is purely a means of deterring the bad actors and ensuring legitimate trading for players.

'''Battery Weapons''' (or '''Rechargeable Weapons''') are those that have their [[magazine]] automatically replenish over time after an initial delay when the weapon stops firing, without any need to manually [[reload]]. These weapons cannot pick up [[ammo]] packs nor have reserve ammo. The battery regenerates a set amount of ammo based on the weapon, thus [[Magazine Capacity]] affects the amount of time to fully replenish ammo. [[Reload Speed]] bonuses only affect the '''recharge delay''', while the '''recharge rate''' cannot be changed. Players can interrupt the full recharge process by firing the partially recharged weapon.

All [[Archgun]]s in [[Archwing]] or held by [[Necramech]]s have auto-recharging functions. However, when called down by an [[Archgun Deployer]] for atmospheric combat, they instead have standard reload and reserve ammo.

==Differences With Reloadable Weapons==
*[[Reload Speed]] bonuses only affect the '''recharge delay''' on battery weapons. It will not increase the rate at which a weapon regain ammo.
*Not affected by [[Ammo Maximum]] bonuses since they have no reserve ammo.
*0 [[Ammo Pickup]] stat.
*Reload key does not do anything.
*Ammo can still recharge during [[Maneuvers]] (e.g. [[rolling]], [[Bullet Jump]]).
*Ammo can still recharge while [[holster]]ed.
*Ammo can still recharge after being [[Knockdown]].
*Ammo recharge is not affected by slow down effects like {{D|Cold}} procs.

==List of Battery Weapons==
See [[:Category:Battery Weapons]]

=== Notable weapons ===
These Battery Weapons exist in categories which typically require ammo, and may be useful alternatives if you are concerned with running out of ammo during certain activities.

* Primary
** {{Weapon|Basmu}}
** {{Weapon|Bubonico}} / {{Weapon|Coda Bubonico}}
** {{Weapon|Flux Rifle}} (Non-Tenet version only)
** {{Weapon|Fulmin}} / {{Weapon|Fulmin Prime}}
** {{Weapon|Haalvu}}
** {{Weapon|Shedu}}
** Any Primary [[Kitgun]] using {{Arcane|Pax Charge}}
* Secondary
** {{Weapon|Cycron}} / {{Weapon|Tenet Cycron}}
** {{Weapon|Plinx}} / {{Weapon|Tenet Plinx}}
** Any Secondary [[Kitgun]] using {{Arcane|Pax Charge}}

==Upgrades That Can Convert Weapons Into Battery Weapons==
*{{Arcane|Pax Charge}} for [[Kitgun]]s

Is {{A|Crush}}, {{A|Magnetize}}, and {{A|Tornado}} DoT?}} '''Damage over Time''' (or '''DoT''') describes effects that periodically deal [[damage]] to targets over a set period of time. As opposed to applying damaging effects upon hitting the target's [[hitbox]], DoT effects will deal damage per tick until the DoT duration ends. A DoT tick typically lasts 1 second and may be applied upon DoT trigger without delay. DoT damage can be ignored if the target becomes [[invulnerable]] during the DoT effect or if the associated Status Effect is cleansed prematurely. The total damage a DoT deals from [[Status Effect]]s is indicated by a green indicator on the target's [[Health]]/[[Shield]]/{{D|Overguard}} bar, which darkens if enough DoTs are applied to kill the target. ==Damage over Time Effects== ===Status Effects=== These [[Status Effect]]s deal DoT when procced: {| class="wikitable" |- ! DoT duration, {{A|Sickening Pulse}} will extend active DoT Status Effects by creating a new proc instance with new timers. ==Calculating Damage Over Time== {{Main|Damage/Calculation#Damage Over Time Final Calculations}} {| class="wikitable" |- | { \text{Total Ticks} = \lfloor \text{Tick Rate} \times (\text{Duration} - \text{Delay Time}) \rfloor + 1 } | *Tick Rate for most effects is 1 tick per second. |- | { \text{Total Damage over Time} = \text{Damage per Tick} \times \text{Total Ticks} } | *Damage per Tick is affected by sources of Status Damage bonus |- |} For example, when an ability deals 600 damage per tick and it ticks twice per second, the ability will deal 1,200 damage per second. In other words, the ability has a DoT of 1,200. Tick rates vary across DoT sources. In the example above the tick rate was 2s-1, which is a common rate for DoT from Warframe abilities. For {{D|Bleed}} DoT, damage ticks 6 times over a 6 second duration; this results in a tick rate of 1s-1, and the same applies to all DoT from Status Effects. If the tick rate does not divide into the total duration evenly, the total number of ticks dealt is rounded down. For example, with a tick rate of 2s-1 and a total duration of 3.4s, the first tick will occur at 0 seconds, with each subsequent tick occurring every 0.5 seconds until 3 seconds have passed. The last tick occurs here because the 3.4 second duration ends before the next tick can occur at the 3.5 second mark. As such, the total number of ticks that occurred is 7. ==DoT Damage Scaling== If the initial hit is affected by the following, a resulting damage-dealing effect will also benefit accordingly: *[[Buff & Debuff|Damage Buffs]] and relevant [[Mods]]. **This includes for example total damage multipliers (e.g. {{M|Furious Javelin}}, {{A|Eclipse}}), additive damage bonuses (e.g. {{M|Serration}} or {{A|Vex Armor}}), and enemy debuffs (e.g. {{A|Molecular Prime}}, {{A|Rest & Rage}}). ***Weakspots generated by {{A|Sonar}} or {{M|Detect Vulnerability}} only increase damage of the initial hit, '''not''' the resulting proc damage. *Relevant elemental damage [[Mods]] (e.g. {{M|Hellfire}}, {{M|Malignant Force}}). **This only applies to elemental status effects, mods like {{M|Sawtooth Clip}} do not buff {{D|Slash}} status damage. **DoTs of combined status effects (i.e. {{D|Gas}}, {{D|Blast}}) are '''not''' buffed by their component mods (e.g. {{M|Thermite Rounds}}+{{M|Infected Clip}}). ***The only way to buff them is by using literal elemental damage (e.g. {{M|Leaded Gas}}, {{M|Valence Formation}}). ***This also works in reverse. For example: using {{A|Toxic Lash}} with {{D|Corrosive}} mods (e.g. {{M|Infected Clip}} and {{M|Stormbringer}}) '''will''' buff the forced {{D|Toxin}} DoT. *[[Critical Hit]]s and [[Stealth#Stealth Damage Bonus|Stealth Damage Bonus]]. *[[Status Damage]] bonuses (e.g. {{M|Rifle Elementalist}}). *[[Melee#Combo Counter|Melee Combo Counter]] and [[Sniper Rifle|Sniper Combo Counter]]. *[[Enemy Body Parts|Body part multipliers]]. *[[Faction Damage Bonus]] (e.g. {{M|Bane of Infested}}, {{A|Roar}}). **Due to the nature of Faction Damage Bonuses, they are applied once more during the calculation of damaging status effects, even though they already affect the initial hit. ***For example: a weapon with an innate '''100''' damage modded with {{M|Serration}} and {{M|Bane of Grineer}}, a {{D|Slash}} proc will deal the following damage per tick:
'''{{Math|Bleed per tick {{eql}} 100 {{mul}} (1 + {{M|Serration|1.65}}) {{mul}} {{text||0.35|hover=0.35 is the multiplier for Bleed ticks.}} {{mul}} (1 + {{M|Bane of Grineer|0.3}}) {{text||^2|hover=Faction Damage gets applied twice for this.}} {{mul}} (1 + {{M|Rifle Elementalist|0.9}})|t=y}}''' ==DoT Detonation== DoT effects may end prematurely but apply all of their damage ticks in a single damage instance under these effects: *{{A|Expedite Suffering}} *{{A|Final Verse}} (Tragedy) *{{M|Divine Retribution}} *{{Weapon|Harmony}} Heavy Attack ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|43}} ;Damage Over Time Preview Damage Over Time (DOT) Status Effects are now reflected by a new “Damage Over Time Preview” indicator on healthbars, showcasing the exact amount of damage they will deal over their duration. *This new indicator will display the damage that will be dealt across Health, Shields, and/or Overguard. *Damage Over Time that applies lethal damage will result in a black outline around the health bar. *This indicator only applies to DOT from Status Effects, not Abilities that deal damage over time. **Ex: Damage from Saryn’s Spores will not be reflected in this new indicator, but damage from the Status Effects dealt by Koumei’s Bunraku will. *Players can change the color of this indicator via the Customize Hud Colors screen in the Accessibility settings. }} {{DamageNav}} [[Category:Mechanics]] [[Category:Damage]]
